## Summary
Briefly describe the bug in 1 to 3 sentences.

## Why this matters
Explain the impact of the bug.
Examples: broken workflow, incorrect behaviour, failed validation, bad UX, failing build, security concern.

## Area affected
Which part of the project is affected?
Examples: frontend, backend, database, devops, docs, repo setup. (Also remember to add the correct `area:xyz` label to the issue.)

## Current behaviour
What happens now?
Be specific about the incorrect behaviour.

## Expected behaviour
What should happen instead?

## Steps to reproduce
List the shortest reliable steps to reproduce the issue.
1. 
2. 
3. 

## Scope/Affected files
List the files, folders, components, services, endpoints, queries, or workflows that are likely involved.
Examples:
- `apps/web/...`
- `apps/api/...`
- `packages/shared/...`
- specific component/service/controller names

## Evidence
Include anything that will help another developer diagnose the issue.
Examples:
- logs
- screenshots
- error messages
- failing tests
- request/response samples
- stack traces

## Suspected cause (optional)
If you have a likely cause, note it here.

## Proposed fix (optional)
If you already have an idea of how to fix it, note it here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The bug is fixed
- [ ] The expected behaviour is confirmed
- [ ] Relevant files/components/services were updated as needed
- [ ] Relevant tests were added or updated if applicable
- [ ] Existing related behaviour still works
- [ ] Any required documentation was updated if applicable

## Additional notes
Anything else the team should know.
